sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, on Monday morning, two rival bosses showed up for work at the federal government's top consumer protection agency.
sentences.zh: 今天，周一上午，两位敌对的领导同时出现在联邦政府最高消费者保护机构的办公室。

sentences.en: Why a nominee of President Trump and an Obama holdover are publicly and messily fighting for control of an agency that Democrats in Washington love and Republicans hate.
sentences.zh: 为什么特朗普总统提名的候选人和奥巴马时期的留任者，要为了争夺一个华盛顿民主党人喜爱、共和党人痛恨的机构的控制权，而进行公开且混乱的斗争？

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月28日，星期二。

sentences.en: Gary, where did the idea for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau first come from?
sentences.zh: 加里，消费者金融保护局的构想最初是怎么来的？

sentences.en: So, Elizabeth Warren, then a law professor at Harvard, wrote a paper in an obscure journal in 2007 saying maybe there should be a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
sentences.zh: 当时在哈佛大学担任法学教授的伊丽莎白·沃伦在2007年的一本冷门期刊上发表了一篇论文，提出或许应该设立一个消费者金融保护局，

sentences.en: just like there's a Consumer Product Protection Bureau.
sentences.zh: 就像已经有了消费者产品保护局一样。

sentences.en: Gary Rivlin has been reporting on the agency since its beginning.
sentences.zh: 加里·里夫林从该机构成立之初就开始进行报道。

sentences.en: And what does this paper that Warren writes from her perch as an academic, what does it actually envision?
sentences.zh: 那么沃伦以学者身份撰写的这篇论文，它到底设想了什么？

sentences.en: There would be an agency for the federal government that looked out for the rights of people in their financial decisions, just like there's a product safety division,
sentences.zh: 它设想联邦政府应该设立一个机构，在人们做财务决策时保护他们的权利，就像有一个产品安全部门一样，

sentences.en: an agency that makes sure that our toasters are safe and don't blow up in our kitchen.
sentences.zh: 一个确保我们的烤面包机安全、不会在厨房里爆炸的机构。

sentences.en: So her idea is like, hey, for a $20 toaster, we have this agency.
sentences.zh: 所以她的想法是，嘿，对于一台20美元的烤面包机，我们都有这样的机构。

sentences.en: What about for a $200,000 mortgage that can really destroy someone's life if it explodes?
sentences.zh: 那对于一笔如果出问题真能毁掉一个人生活的20万美元抵押贷款，又该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: And what's happened to home mortgage foreclosures over the last 25 years?
sentences.zh: 过去25年里，住房抵押贷款止赎情况发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: They're up three and a half fold.
sentences.zh: 增加了三倍半。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: You know, that's remarkable, particularly because interest rates are low today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很引人注目，尤其是考虑到现在的利率很低。

sentences.en: And does anyone in Washington pay particular attention at the time to this paper and to this idea that this Harvard professor has for protecting American consumers
sentences.zh: 当时华盛顿有人特别关注这篇论文，以及这位哈佛教授提出的保护美国消费者免受

sentences.en: from financial products that might hurt them?
sentences.zh: 可能伤害他们的金融产品侵害的想法吗？

sentences.en: You know, I'm sure the think tank folks, but I'm not sure where it would have gone if it wasn't for the financial crisis we had a year later.
sentences.zh: 我想智库的人肯定关注了，但如果不是因为一年后发生的金融危机，我不知道这事会走向何方。

sentences.en: Suddenly this idea from a then barely known academic took on a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这位当时几乎默默无闻的学者的想法有了自己的生命力。

sentences.en: The stock market is now down 21%.
sentences.zh: 股市现在下跌了21%。

sentences.en: We're now down 43%.
sentences.zh: 我们现在下跌了43%。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the speed with which we are watching this market deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈我们目睹市场恶化的速度。

sentences.en: Who knows where this is going to end up?
sentences.zh: 谁知道这会以什么收场？

sentences.en: I mean, this is volatility.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是波动性。

sentences.en: We haven't seen, of course, since way before you and I were born.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是你我出生前很久都没见过的。

sentences.en: Two-year note yields went from 190 to 166 in the blink of an eye.
sentences.zh: 两年期国债收益率在眨眼间从190降到了166。

sentences.en: You know what, right now, breaking news here.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，现在有突发新闻。

sentences.en: Stocks all around the world are tanking because of the crisis on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 全球股市因为华尔街的危机而暴跌。

sentences.en: Suddenly Congress had to act.
sentences.zh: 国会不得不立即采取行动。

sentences.en: Marty Frank from Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州的马蒂·弗兰克。

sentences.en: This is a continuation of the markup that began yesterday on 3126.
sentences.zh: 这是昨天开始的关于3126号法案修订工作的延续。

sentences.en: I will ask everybody to take a seat.
sentences.zh: 请大家就座。

sentences.en: He was the chair then of the House Financial Services Committee.
sentences.zh: 他当时是众议院金融服务委员会的主席。

sentences.en: He takes Elizabeth Warren's idea for this Consumer Financial Protection Commission and puts it into his version of Dodd-Frank, which is this sprawling, multifaceted legislation
sentences.zh: 他采纳了伊丽莎白·沃伦关于设立消费者金融保护委员会的想法，并将其纳入了他版本的《多德-弗兰克法案》中，这是一项庞大且多方面的立法，

sentences.en: that looks at derivatives and mortgages and this omnibus thing that includes everything.
sentences.zh: 涵盖了衍生品、抵押贷款等方方面面，是一个包罗万象的法案。

sentences.en: And, you know, one section of it was the Consumer Financial Protection Commission.
sentences.zh: 其中一个章节就是消费者金融保护委员会。

sentences.en: But this is the central issue.
sentences.zh: 但这才是核心问题。

sentences.en: The question is, do you continue consumer protection as it has been?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你是否要像过去那样继续进行消费者保护？

sentences.en: That is, is consumer protection to be left in the hands of agencies for whom it has been and will continue to be a secondary concern at best?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，消费者保护工作是否要继续留在那些将其视为次要关注点的机构手中？

sentences.en: That would do more or less what Elizabeth Warren, professor, laid out in her paper.
sentences.zh: 那基本上就是伊丽莎白·沃伦教授在论文中提出的方案。

sentences.en: It's kind of an obscure academics fantasy that an academic paper like this could become so real so faSt.
sentences.zh: 像这样一篇学术论文能如此迅速地变成现实，简直是冷门学者的幻想。

sentences.en: I've had that same thought.
sentences.zh: 我也曾有过同样的想法。

sentences.en: I mean, how many of these papers are written?
sentences.zh: 我是说，到底写了多少这样的论文？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, it's called democracy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是所谓的民主。

sentences.en: I mean, I've never even heard of this journal.
sentences.zh: 我甚至从没听说过这本期刊。

sentences.en: How many papers are written that are perfectly valid ideas and maybe even great ideas that just sit on a shelf?
sentences.zh: 有多少论文提出了完全合理甚至伟大的想法，却最终被束之高阁？

sentences.en: But, you know, sometimes it's timing, right?
sentences.zh: 但有时候，时机很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, she wrote it a year before the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 她是在金融危机前一年写的。

sentences.en: The consumer agency that we propose would have consumer protection as its major concern.
sentences.zh: 我们提议的消费者机构将把消费者保护作为其主要关注点。

sentences.en: In fact, it's only concern in terms of its enforcement.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在执法方面，这是它唯一的关注点。

sentences.en: And what sort of powers is this new bureau given in the wake of the financial crisis by Congress as it's being created?
sentences.zh: 在金融危机之后，国会在创建这个新局时赋予了它什么样的权力？

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, it's just remarkable powers.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这些权力简直非同寻常。

sentences.en: It's a strong single director rather than a five-person commission as it was originally conceived.
sentences.zh: 它由一位强有力的单一局长领导，而不是最初设想的五人委员会。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren, professor, talked about a commission, a five-person commission that would have to debate every big decision and sometimes there are vacancies
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦教授谈到的是一个委员会，一个必须对每一项重大决策进行辩论的五人委员会，有时会出现空缺，

sentences.en: and sometimes there are splits.
sentences.zh: 有时会出现意见分歧。

sentences.en: Instead, this idea that you have a single director that could act as he or she sees fit means everything to the CFPB.
sentences.zh: 相反，这种由单一局长根据自己的判断行事的想法，对消费者金融保护局来说意味着一切。

sentences.en: So beyond the financial crisis, what are the political circumstances that allowed the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
sentences.zh: 那么除了金融危机之外，还有哪些政治环境促成了消费者金融保护局的

sentences.en: to actually get created and have the power that it has?
sentences.zh: 真正建立并拥有它现在的权力？

sentences.en: It was this incredible moment where there was a popular new president in the White House.
sentences.zh: 那是一个不可思议的时刻，白宫里有一位受欢迎的新总统。

sentences.en: The Democrats ran the House.
sentences.zh: 民主党控制了众议院。

sentences.en: The Democrats had 59 votes.
sentences.zh: 民主党拥有59票。

sentences.en: They had a Senate, nearly a supermajority in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有参议院，在参议院几乎拥有绝对多数。

sentences.en: And there was just this window.
sentences.zh: 当时正好有这样一个窗口期。

sentences.en: They were about to lose it in a few months, we now know.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，他们几个月后就要失去这个优势了。

sentences.en: And there was this just magic moment where something like the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau could possibly pass because everything was lined up.
sentences.zh: 那是一个神奇的时刻，像消费者金融保护局这样的机构才有可能通过，因为一切条件都具备了。

sentences.en: Not that it wasn't a huge fight.
sentences.zh: 并不是说这没有经过激烈的斗争。

sentences.en: And in the end, it was a 60 to 38 vote.
sentences.zh: 最终，投票结果是60票对38票。

sentences.en: You had one Democrat, Russ Feingold, voting against it.
sentences.zh: 有一位民主党人拉斯·范戈尔德投了反对票。

sentences.en: And you had three Republicans,
sentences.zh: 有三位共和党人，

sentences.en: Scott Brown, Olympia Snow, and Susan Collins voting for it.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·布朗、奥林匹亚·斯诺和苏珊·柯林斯投了赞成票。

sentences.en: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau will be a watchdog for the American consumer.
sentences.zh: 消费者金融保护局将成为美国消费者的守护者。

sentences.en: But, you know, 60 to 38 went right down to the wire like these things tend to go.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，60对38的投票结果就像这类事情一样，一直僵持到最后一刻。

sentences.en: I'm proud that we got this done.
sentences.zh: 我为我们完成了这件事感到自豪。

sentences.en: And I'm equally proud that Elizabeth Warren will be helping to make her original vision a reality.
sentences.zh: 我也同样为伊丽莎白·沃伦将帮助把她最初的愿景变为现实感到自豪。

sentences.en: So we are extremely proud of you, Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们为你感到无比自豪，伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: Good luck.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: It was presumed at that point that Obama was going to name
sentences.zh: 当时人们普遍认为奥巴马会任命

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren the first commissioner as her baby.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦为首任局长，因为这是她的心血结晶。

sentences.en: She was there creating it.
sentences.zh: 是她一手创建了它。

sentences.en: So naturally, she should become the first director.
sentences.zh: 所以理所当然，她应该成为第一任局长。

sentences.en: But here on Wall Street, the woman who is likely to lead America's new consumer protection agency is highly unpopular.
sentences.zh: 但在这里华尔街，这位可能领导美国新消费者保护机构的女性非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Once it was decided that Elizabeth Warren was too hot to handle, she was just too controversial.
sentences.zh: 一旦决定伊丽莎白·沃伦太难驾驭，她就太具争议性了。

sentences.en: Barack Obama, around a year after the creation of the CFPB,
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马在消费者金融保护局成立一年左右后，

sentences.en: names Richard Cordray as the director.
sentences.zh: 任命理查德·科德雷为局长。

sentences.en: I should also point out that he took this job, which meant being away from his wife and 12-year-old twins back in Ohio, because he believed so deeply in the mission of the Bureau.
sentences.zh: 我还应该指出，他接受了这份工作，这意味着要离开他在俄亥俄州的妻子和12岁的双胞胎，因为他深信该局的使命。

sentences.en: So once this agency is operational
sentences.zh: 那么一旦这个机构开始运作

sentences.en: and has a leader, what does the Consumer
sentences.zh: 并有了领导人，消费者

sentences.en: Financial Protection Bureau actually do?
sentences.zh: 金融保护局到底做了什么？

sentences.en: So I think the big banking interests thought that the CFPB was going to take on the payday lenders and debt collectors and all the fringe players that most of us could agree
sentences.zh: 我认为大银行利益集团以为消费者金融保护局会去对付发薪日贷款机构、债务催收公司以及所有我们大多数人都同意的边缘参与者，

sentences.en: are abusing consumers with the interest rates they're charging, the terms they're putting on their deals.
sentences.zh: 他们利用高额利率和苛刻的交易条款在侵害消费者。

sentences.en: But, you know, within a couple of years, they started taking on the biggest banks.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，几年之内，他们就开始对付最大的银行了。

sentences.en: Now, the New York Times reports U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在，《纽约时报》报道称，包括消费者

sentences.en: regulators, including the Consumer
sentences.zh: 金融保护局在内的美国

sentences.en: Financial Protection Bureau, are set to fine
sentences.zh: 监管机构准备最早在下个月对

sentences.en: J.P.
sentences.zh: 摩根大通

sentences.en: Morgan
sentences.zh: 处以

sentences.en: $80 million as soon as next month.
sentences.zh: 8000万美元的罚款。

sentences.en: The Consumer Financial
sentences.zh: 消费者金融

sentences.en: Protection Bureau fined Wells Fargo
sentences.zh: 保护局在9月份对富国银行

sentences.en: $185 million in September.
sentences.zh: 处以了1.85亿美元的罚款。

sentences.en: The Consumer Financial
sentences.zh: 消费者金融

sentences.en: Protection Bureau is ordering Citi to pay a total of $770 million.
sentences.zh: 保护局责令花旗银行总共支付7.7亿美元。

sentences.en: In fact, between 2011 and the end of 2016, the CFPB has returned nearly $12 billion to 29 million consumers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，从2011年到2016年底，消费者金融保护局已经为2900万消费者追回了近120亿美元。

sentences.en: So, obviously, in the most black and white terms, this agency is pro-consumer and perhaps anti-business.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，从最黑白分明的角度来看，这个机构是亲消费者的，或许也是反商业的。

sentences.en: From the beginning, are most Republicans adamantly opposed to this agency?
sentences.zh: 从一开始，大多数共和党人就坚决反对这个机构吗？

sentences.en: Or is the moment after the financial crisis one where both Democrats and Republicans agree that this sort of remedy is necessary?
sentences.zh: 还是说金融危机后的那一刻，民主党和共和党都认为这种补救措施是必要的？

sentences.en: The outrage from Senate Republicans was instantaneous.
sentences.zh: 参议院共和党人的愤怒是即时的。

sentences.en: Republicans from the start opposed the CFPB.
sentences.zh: 共和党人从一开始就反对消费者金融保护局。

sentences.en: What conservatives say, the CFPB is BFB, bad for business.
sentences.zh: 保守派称，消费者金融保护局是“对商业有害的”。

sentences.en: Republicans took over the House in 2011.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在2011年接管了众议院。

sentences.en: And so, the House
sentences.zh: 因此，众议院

sentences.en: Financial Services went from
sentences.zh: 金融服务委员会从

sentences.en: Democrat to Republican.
sentences.zh: 民主党手中转到了共和党手中。

sentences.en: And all told, from 2011 to today, there have been
sentences.zh: 总而言之，从2011年至今，已经有

sentences.en: 134 bills aimed at killing or weakening the CFPB.
sentences.zh: 134项旨在废除或削弱消费者金融保护局的法案。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It is a good day on the floor of the House.
sentences.zh: 这对众议院来说是重要的一天。

sentences.en: We will take up and pass the Choice Act, which repeals the Dodd-Frank, which takes the CFPB.
sentences.zh: 我们将审议并通过《选择法案》，该法案废除了《多德-弗兰克法案》，并针对消费者金融保护局。

sentences.en: The House bill that tackles a key issue that I've been sounding the alarm about since my first day in Congress, ending the reckless overreach of Elizabeth Warren's
sentences.zh: 众议院法案解决了我从进入国会第一天起就一直在敲响警钟的关键问题，即结束伊丽莎白·沃伦的

sentences.en: Consumer Financial
sentences.zh: 消费者金融

sentences.en: Protection Bureau.
sentences.zh: 保护局那种鲁莽的越权行为。

sentences.en: The CFPB's concentration of enormous executive power in a single, unaccountable, unchecked director not only departs from settled historical practice, but also poses
sentences.zh: 消费者金融保护局将巨大的行政权力集中在一位不受问责、不受制约的单一局长手中，这不仅背离了既定的历史惯例，而且还构成了

sentences.en: a far greater risk to arbitrary decision-making and abuse of power.
sentences.zh: 导致武断决策和权力滥用的更大风险。

sentences.en: By my math, given what you just said, under Republican control, the House has tried to get rid of this
sentences.zh: 按照我的计算，鉴于你刚才所说的，在共和党控制下，众议院试图废除这个

sentences.en: Consumer Financial
sentences.zh: 消费者金融

sentences.en: Protection Bureau more times than it's tried to get rid of the Affordable
sentences.zh: 保护局的次数，比试图废除《平价

sentences.en: Care Act.
sentences.zh: 医疗法案》的次数还要多。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的很惊人。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, the fight over Dodd-Frank and the CFPB in particular would be the Affordable
